newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador extends bidding deadline for Emetel sale.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador extends bidding deadline for Emetel sale.

text.p: Ecuador extended for the second time the deadline for bids due in an international tender for the sale of 35 percent of state telephone company Emetel, officials said Tuesday.
A spokesman at the National Council for the Modernization of the State told Reuters the bidding has been extended to November 29 from October 30.
The extension is intended to allow more international companies the opportunity to enter the bidding process.
The source said 19 European, U.S. and Asian firms had expressed interest in the Emetel stake so far.
"There has been a large amount of international interest. It was thought pertinent to extend the period," said the spokesman.

GTE Corp, SBC Communications Inc, Korea Telecom, Bell Atlantic Corp, France Telecom, Telefonica de Espana SA, STET International, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and British Telecommunications Plc were among the potential bidders, according to a list given to Reuters by the council.
Emetel is to be split into two units with 35 percent of each offered to investors ahead of the privatization.

Ecuador's government is hoping to raise up to six times the total book value of Emetel through the sale. The total book value of the company is estimated at $800 million, according to international consultants.
